reforms.description: The U.S. federal government committed to increased public expenditure for basic and civilian research and development as part of structural reform initiatives. The federal government sponsors approximately half of total national R&D investment (1.5% of GNP), with plans to increase support for civilian R&D faster than defence-oriented R&D going forward to improve overall R&D productivity and commercial orientation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D funding and reallocation from defence to civilian research enhances productivity, innovation capacity, and commercial applications, supporting long-term GDP growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Description [5] explicitly states 'plans to increase' (future commitment); descriptions [0] and [3] describe ongoing or committed policies.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural reorientation of federal R&D spending priorities and commitment to increased civilian research funding represents a system-wide policy shift with significant macroeconomic implications.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government has been actively involved in sponsoring this type of research, to the extent that half of total national investment in R&D (amounting to about 1½ per cent of GNP) is paid for by the federal government.

reforms.description: The 1988 Trade Act created the National Advisory Committee on Semiconductors (Sematech) to ensure U.S. supremacy in semiconductor technology and mandated creation of a national commission on superconductivity to promote U.S. leadership in that area.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted sectoral R&D in semiconductors and superconductivity addresses strategic technology gaps and supports competitive advantage in high-value industries, enhancing long-term productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The 1988 Trade Act created these institutions; status is implemented as of the 1990 survey date.
reforms.importance_rationale: Creation of major sectoral R&D institutions (Sematech, superconductivity commission) through legislation represents a structural policy intervention in critical technology domains.
reforms.source_quote: The 1988 Trade Act took a step towards intervention by creating a National Advisory Committee on Semiconductors (Sematech), with the aim of ensuring U.S. supremacy in semiconductor technology. It also mandated the creation of a national commission on superconductivity in order to promote U.S. leadership in this area.

reforms.description: Congress expanded the Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) mandate to provide venture capital funding for government-industry consortia developing advanced technologies including semiconductors, high-definition television (HDTV), superconductivity, and artificial intelligence.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: DARPA venture capital provision supports commercialisation of advanced technologies and enables startup formation in strategic sectors, fostering innovation ecosystems and competitive advantage.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Congress expanded DARPA's mandate' and describes active funding flows, indicating implementation by 1990 survey date.
reforms.importance_rationale: Expansion of DARPA's mandate to include venture capital represents a significant structural change in how government supports applied R&D and technology commercialisation.
reforms.source_quote: Subsequently funds have been channelled into high-definition television (HDTV), superconductivity and artificial intelligence through the Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA), which finances the government-industry consortium for developing semiconductor manufacturing technology. Congress expanded DARPA's mandate to allow it to provide venture capital.

reforms.description: The federal government has managed defence-related R&D (0.8% of GNP, reaching 66% of total R&D by 1989) with explicit focus on exploiting commercial applications, generating significant advances in civil aviation, medical technology, lasers, integrated circuits, and weather satellites.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Systematic commercialisation of defence R&D spillovers into civil applications (aviation, medical, electronics) enhances overall innovation productivity and creates positive externalities across multiple sectors.
reforms.status_evidence: Text uses past tense ('has managed') and cites 1989 data, indicating ongoing implementation as of survey date.
reforms.importance_rationale: Describes an established policy approach to defence R&D commercialisation rather than a new reform; significant in scope but not a structural change.
reforms.source_quote: Defence R&D activities have been managed so as to exploit commercial applications. Significant advances in civil aviation and medical technology have had their origin in defence-sponsored R&D, as have civilian use of lasers, integrated circuits and weather satellites.
